data.title: A2 Progress Check
data.description: A second mixed grammar check to measure progress and confirm whether the learner is working securely at CEFR A2 level.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct sentence using an adverb of frequency.
sections.explain: Adverbs such as 'usually' normally come before the main verb. The correct form is 'usually walks'.

words.word: He usually walks to work.
He walks usually to work.
He usually walk to work.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence describing an action happening now.
sections.explain: For something happening now, use 'am/is/are' + verb-ing. The correct form is 'are waiting'.

words.word: They are waiting for the bus.
They waiting for the bus.
They are wait for the bus.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct negative sentence in the past simple.
sections.explain: Past simple negatives use 'did not' or 'didn't' followed by the base form of the verb. The correct form is 'didn't buy'.

words.word: I didn't buy anything at the shop.
I didn't bought anything at the shop.
I don't bought anything at the shop.

sections.explain: The superlative of 'good' is 'best'. We normally use 'the' before a superlative.

words.word: This is the best restaurant in town.
This is the better restaurant in town.
This is the most good restaurant in town.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct expression of quantity.
sections.explain: Use 'many' with countable plural nouns such as 'people'.

words.word: There weren't many people at the party.
There weren't much people at the party.
There wasn't many people at the party.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct modal verb structure.
sections.explain: After 'can', use the base form of the verb without 'to'. The correct form is 'can speak'.

words.word: My sister can speak three languages.
My sister can speaks three languages.
My sister can to speak three languages.

sections.explain: The verb 'want' is followed by 'to' + the base form of the verb. The correct form is 'want to learn'.

words.word: I want to learn how to drive.
I want learning how to drive.
I want learn how to drive.

sections.explain: Use 'will' + the base form of the verb for a simple future prediction. The correct form is 'will be'.

words.word: I think the weather will be better tomorrow.
I think the weather will is better tomorrow.
I think the weather will to be better tomorrow.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct present perfect form.
sections.explain: Use 'have/has' + past participle with 'already'. The past participle of 'eat' is 'eaten'.

words.word: She has already eaten lunch.
She has already ate lunch.
She already has eat lunch.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence comparing a past event with the present.
sections.explain: Use the past simple with a finished past time such as 'last year'. The correct form is 'visited ... last year'.

words.word: We visited France last year.
We have visited France last year.
We have visit France last year.
